To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

targeted sequencing of MODY genes in a large cohort of Brazilian individuals with monogenic diabetes identified novel variants in common MODY genes and in rare MODY genes, and that these novel variants are associated with a clinical phenotype consistent with the MODY phenotype.

1) the most frequent variants in common MODY genes were HNF1A and GCK, 2) the most frequent rare variants were in HNF1A, HNF4A and PDX1, 3) HNF1A mutations were more frequent in patients with diabetes onset before 20 years, and 4) HNF4A mutations were more prevalent in patients with diabetes associated to obesity and/or insulin resistance.
we identified novel variants in MODY genes and that we identified a new MODY gene.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the detection and analysis of DNA methylation.
the study of the molecular genetics of MODY in the Brazilian population.
the identification of new genetic variants in MODY‐X and other MODY subtypes in the Brazilian population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most common MODY genes are HNF1A, GCK, and PDX1.
there are no specific clinical characteristics to distinguish between MODY and T1D.
the genetic etiology of the MODY phenotype is not well understood in Brazil and that a more comprehensive approach should be considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified novel pathogenic variants in common and less common MODY genes, and that the most frequent cause of MODY was GCK, followed by HNF4A, and that we found a novel MODY gene in Brazil.

the prevalence of MODY‐X is high in our cohort, with 40% of the cases being diagnosed as such, and that the use of targeted sequencing in MODY screening is feasible and efficient, allowing the identification of novel variants.
targeted next‐generation sequencing (NGS) is an effective strategy to identify novel variants in common (HNF1A, GCK) and rare (NEUROG3, HNF4A, PDX1, INS, HNF1B, CEL, KCNJ11, ABCC8) MODY genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
targeted sequencing of the 11 MODY genes can identify novel variants and improve the diagnosis of MODY in Brazil.
targeted sequencing can identify novel variants in common (HNF1A, GCK) and rare MODY (NEUROD1, PDX1, HNF1B, ABCC8, HNF4A and INS) genes.
